routes.label: Compare multiples of one positive power
Bound every other choice by V

question: Let \(U = 2 \cdot 2004^{2005},\) \(V = 2004^{2005},\) \(W = 2003 \cdot 2004^{2004},\) \(X = 2 \cdot 2004^{2004},\) \(Y = 2004^{2004}\) and \(Z = 2004^{2003}.\) Which of the following is largest?
solution:
The large powers become manageable if we express every choice using the same positive factor. Let \(T=2004^{2004}>0\). Then \(2004^{2005}=2004T\) and \(2004^{2003}=T/2004\), so
\[
\begin{aligned}
U-V&=2004T,\\
V-W&=(2004-2003)T=T,\\
W-X&=(2003-2)T=2001T,\\
X-Y&=(2-1)T=T,\\
Y-Z&=\left(1-\frac1{2004}\right)T.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(T\) is positive, comparing these quantities is the same as comparing their coefficients. The coefficient \(2004\) exceeds \(2001\), \(1\), and \(1-1/2004<1\). Therefore \(U-V\) is largest, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Since \(U=2V\), the first choice is \(U-V=V\). It is enough to show that each other choice is smaller than \(V\).

All six quantities are positive. Also,
\[
W=2003\cdot2004^{2004}
<2004\cdot2004^{2004}=V,
\]
and \(Y=2004^{2004}<V\). Using these facts and \(X=2Y\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
V-W&<V,\\
W-X&<W<V,\\
X-Y&=Y<V,\\
Y-Z&<Y<V.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus every other choice is less than \(U-V\). The largest is \(U-V\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
